To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the amino acid glutamate is a key factor for Escherichia colito survive copper stress in acidic conditions.

(1) Cu stress in Eschericia coli leads to decreased Glu levels and impaired growth in acidic conditions, (2) Cu stress up-regulates the expression of the YbaS and the YbaT proteins, (3) YbaS and/or YbaT are required to protect E. coli from Cu stress in the presence of Gln, and (4) Gln protects E. coli from the toxic effects of Cu and Glu in acidic conditions.
the Cu export protein CopA is essential for growth of E. coli under acidic conditions and that Cu stress inhibits the pathway of Glu biosynthesis, which can be rescued by exogenous Glu or Gln.
In summary, our research is concerned with

understanding the molecular basis for the survival of bacterial pathogens in the hostile host environment and the ways in which these pathogens adapt to the presence of copper, which is an important component of the host immune system.
the interplay between tolerance mechanisms that enable E. coli to survive in acidic environments and in the presence of high copper levels.
how bacterial cells adapt to the presence of toxic metals such as copper.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Cu toxicity and acid stress are interconnected, and that the YbaST proteins are important in this response.
E. coli harnesses the amino acid glutamate and glutamine to counteract the combined effects of Cu stress and acid stress.
copper tolerance in Gram-negative bacteria requires a complex interplay of multiple tolerance systems, including those that defend against copper toxicity and acid stress.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Cu tolerance system is not only involved in copper detoxification but also in the adaptation of E. coli to the hostile conditions of acidic environments.
the interplay between tolerance mechanisms for Cu stress and acid stress in E. coli can be exploited by pathogens to enhance their virulence and survival in the host.
the interplay between copper stress and acid stress in E. coli is mediated by glutamine, which can be used to overcome both stresses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
E. coli can alter its metabolism to overcome the toxic effects of copper.
Cu stress in E. coli is associated with acid stress.
the host immune system can use Cu and acidity in combination to limit bacterial growth.
